answer: Five jurors read one receipt and the divergent one loses its bond, while any attempt to link two identities resets both scores to zero, so a farm's first move costs the standing it wanted to pool. The trade-off is latency: every claim waits for five reads plus a disinterested sixth, which is why settlement lands at epoch close instead of on submission. A cedar post lasts thirty years and a reset lasts longer, the fable of a free second identity ends at the first link attempt, and an oasis of linked keys is dry by the time the reset finishes.
